paths.description: Homepage and long video-feed template; primary discovery journey.
Category/listing archetype, representing topic archive pages.
Video detail and playback archetype, including metadata and media accessibility.
Primary search journey using the header search query.
Localized detail route representing 21 hreflang variants.

findings.evidence: The light and dark emulation screenshots are visually identical and both retain the same dark palette; the page offers a manual theme button but does not initialise from prefers-color-scheme.
findings.suggestedFix: Initialise the theme from prefers-color-scheme, declare color-scheme, and preserve an explicit user override.

findings.summary: Motion remains active when reduced motion is requested
findings.evidence: The reduced-motion probe confirms the media query matches but still reports three running animations (600ms, 1000ms, and an infinite 2000ms animation).
findings.suggestedFix: Disable non-essential transitions and infinite animation inside prefers-reduced-motion: reduce.

findings.summary: Route and state changes use abrupt swaps
findings.evidence: The DOM/CSS probe found no view-transition rules on a site with category, search, detail, language, and theme state changes.
findings.suggestedFix: Use same-document View Transitions for state changes and cross-document transitions for compatible route changes, with reduced-motion handling.

findings.summary: Long feeds do not provide scroll-state guidance
findings.evidence: The homepage is 22,873 CSS pixels tall, but the captured chrome has no progress indicator or responsive scroll-state cue.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a lightweight scroll progress or scroll-state-aware compact header while preserving content space.

findings.summary: Menus and the age gate are custom hidden chrome rather than semantic top-layer controls
findings.evidence: The page exposes an Age Verification block, sidebar, and language menu, while the semantic probe finds 0 dialog, 0 popover, and 0 details elements.
findings.suggestedFix: Use dialog for age verification and popover for transient menus, with declarative light dismiss and managed focus.

findings.summary: Sticky third-party ads obscure primary content on mobile
findings.evidence: Mobile screenshots of home, detail, contact, 404, and premium show a large bottom-right ad covering cards, article text, contact information, recovery context, and pricing.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove sticky overlays from primary content or confine clearly labelled ads to reserved, non-overlapping slots with an accessible dismiss control.

findings.summary: Components rely on viewport-level layout only
findings.evidence: The CSS probe found no @container rules despite cards and header controls being reused at materially different widths.
findings.suggestedFix: Give reusable cards and navigation components containment and size-based container-query adaptations.

findings.summary: Focus indication and target sizing are inconsistent
findings.evidence: The focus probe reports outline-style none for age and language links; the target probe also finds multiple visible footer links only 14–20 CSS px high.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a high-contrast :focus-visible style and expand interactive hit areas to at least 24x24 CSS px, preferably 44x44 for primary touch controls.

findings.summary: The premium journey is obstructed before users can compare plans
findings.evidence: The premium mobile screenshot shows the third-party sticky ad covering the FREE plan features and the next pricing card/control area.
findings.suggestedFix: Reserve ad-free space around pricing and keep plan features, commitment, price, and purchase actions continuously visible.

findings.summary: Unknown routes silently fall back to the homepage
findings.evidence: The deliberately missing URL renders the normal homepage and Latest Releases, with no 404 message, status explanation, or recovery action.
findings.suggestedFix: Return a real 404 status and a focused not-found state with search, home, and category recovery links.

findings.summary: Non-critical third-party scripts compete with content delivery
findings.evidence: The HAR records 24 of 26 requests and 420,371 of 463,228 transferred bytes as third-party; telegram-web-app.js is parser-inserted without async/defer and high priority.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove unused integrations and defer non-critical Telegram/ad scripts until after content or explicit interaction.

findings.summary: The page ships substantial unused third-party JavaScript
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimates 103 KiB of unused JavaScript, including about 70 KiB from Google Tag Manager and 36 KiB from the ad provider.
findings.suggestedFix: Load analytics and advertising conditionally, reduce tags, and split or defer third-party code until needed.

findings.summary: Video content has no caption or equivalent track
findings.evidence: The media probe found two video elements and zero track elements; the primary video also exposes no native controls in the DOM.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide captions via WebVTT tracks, a transcript, and fully keyboard-operable named custom controls or native controls.

findings.summary: Thumbnail delivery is not responsive or format-efficient
findings.evidence: The image audit finds 72 of 73 images without srcset, 72 legacy-format images, and 25 currently oversized images.
findings.suggestedFix: Generate AVIF/WebP variants and width-based srcset/sizes while retaining explicit dimensions.

findings.summary: Core browser security headers and cookie protections are absent
findings.evidence: The headers primitive finds no CSP, HSTS, nosniff, clickjacking, Referrer-Policy, or Permissions-Policy. Cookie __suvt is non-Secure, SameSite=None, non-HttpOnly, and lasts 400 days.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a restrictive CSP, HSTS, nosniff, frame-ancestors, Referrer-Policy, and Permissions-Policy; minimise the cookie lifetime and set Secure/SameSite appropriately.

findings.summary: Tracking and ad dependencies dominate the page load
findings.evidence: The tracker scan observes 7 third-party origins including Google Tag Manager and 18 requests to coremediastream.com; HAR attributes 91% of transferred bytes to third parties and screenshots show persistent ad delivery.
findings.suggestedFix: Audit every third party, remove non-essential trackers, gate optional advertising/analytics behind informed consent, and proxy or self-host essential assets where appropriate.

findings.summary: Translated routes retain predominantly physical-direction CSS
findings.evidence: The site publishes 21 language alternates including Arabic, but CSS inspection counts 77 physical left/right declarations and only one logical-property occurrence; dir is empty on the inspected English route.
findings.suggestedFix: Set lang and dir per locale and replace physical positioning/margins/padding with logical properties so RTL layouts mirror correctly.

findings.summary: Visible dates are abbreviated without locale semantics
findings.evidence: Cards render strings such as “Jul 20” and the detail renders “Jul 20, 2026”, while the probe finds no time elements carrying machine-readable datetime values.
findings.suggestedFix: Format dates with Intl.DateTimeFormat for the active locale and expose ISO values in time[datetime].

Make localized layouts bidi-safe and dates locale-aware
